docs.text: Happy St. Patrick’s Day from the Emerald Bowfin!☘️🐟 From the Great Lakes to the Gulf Coast, few freshwater fishes are as festive as male bowfins! Their bellies and fins turn bright green during spawning season (right now in parts of their range!)🌎 *Gulf of MEXICO.

Have a holly, jolly (roger) #Fishmas! ☠️🐟 Ahoy from the Pirate Perch (Aphredoderus sayanus), kicking off the first day of #GreatLakes #25DaysofFishmas! This fish is secretive, nocturnal, and has a very… unique anatomy - and it's the answer to this week's #SundayFishSketch mystery theme!

Wait a minute, that’s no fish! 🦞 Day 6 brings the first Grinch of this year’s #25DaysofFishmas + a #Crustmas crossover: one Sandy Claws you don’t want coming to town. The Marbled Crayfish (Procambarus virginalis), AKA Marmorkrebs, is an invasive species that’s been knocking on the #GreatLakes door

It’s #Festivus, so you know what that means - time for an Airing of Grievances about a #GreatLakes Grinch! Goldfish (Carassius auratus) - yes, the goldfish of home aquariums worldwide - have unfortunately been an invasive species in the #GreatLakes for decades #25DaysofFishmas

Day 7 of #Fishmas is all about that bass - the smallmouth bass, that is! One of the most popular sport fish species in the #GreatLakes (and beyond), the Smallmouth Bass (Micropterus dolomieu) - also known by anglers as the bronzeback or brownie - never misses a beat 🎶 #25DaysofFishmas

Day 22’s #25DaysofFishmas feature may look Grinchy, but don’t let that fool you! We say “Oh, hi!” to the Northeast/Great Lakes region + the Ohio Lamprey (Ichthyomyzon bdellium), a parasitic native fish who may seem more suited for Halloween but is full of holiday spirit! (and fish juice, probably)

🎶They call me mellow yellow (bass), quite rightly🎶 Take some time on Day 12 of #25DaysofFishmas to mellow out during the busy #Fishmas season with the Yellow Bass (Morone mississippiensis)! While this species isn't widely found throughout the #GreatLakes region, it's still worthy of a look 💛

In 2022, bowfin was split into 2 separate species after long being recognized as a single species (Amia calva). Those living in the #GreatLakes region were reclassified as Amia ocellicauda + those in the southeastern US stayed Amia calva #25DaysofFishmas royalsocietypublishing.org/doi/10.1098/...
"I'm not a fish!" Says the marbled crayfish on the 6th day of #25DaysOfFishmas.
my #SundayFishSketch is a pirate perch. Arrr! today i learned that this fish, a native of the Great Lakes, has its anus under its throat. nature is weird. #sciart

Pirate perch are found throughout the eastern and central U.S. (including parts of the #GreatLakes region) where they typically live in slow-moving waters with muddy bottoms and a lot of aquatic plants #25DaysofFishmas

Bowfin are a common fish we encounter while sampling #GreatLakes coastal wetlands - not surprising given their love of sluggish, weedy waters. While I love them, they're basically thrashing muscles covered in slime, making handling them ... challenging, to say the least #25DaysofFishmas

Bowfin - is a member of the Bowfins family. It is native to the Great Lakes and Mississippi River basins from Quebec in Canada to northern Minnesota and south to Gulf, and on Atlantic and Gulf coastal plains, USA. It can reach a max length of 109 cm (43 inches). www.redbubble.com/shop/ap/1586...
